clue.text: Arrogant, having been promoted, a matter for regret

parts.note: someone promoted has gone up
'it's a pity' means it is regrettable

explanation.surface: Someone became arrogant after a promotion, which is a shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity is an informal word for self-important, acting above one's station.

clue.text: Managed by mistake to ignore two leaders

indicators.note: the first two letters of the word for mistake are left out

parts.note: a blunder is a mistake

explanation.surface: Something was managed by accident, by skipping two people in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ignore two leaders' drops BL from BLUNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Under, as in 'under new management', means controlled or run by.

clue.text: Capitalist rating business: union record on the up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a rating is an ordinary sailor, a tar
CO is short for company
TU is a trade union
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A financier assesses a company: union membership is rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' looks like a credit score but is a sailor. 'on the up' reverses TARCOTULP.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is a person whose power comes from wealth, a capitalist in the extreme.

clue.text: Up to work checkout

definitions.meaning: a cash register at a checkout

explanation.surface: Someone is up to working on the supermarket checkout.
explanation.definitionFit: Till covers the preposition until, the farming verb, and the shop cash register.

clue.text: Got to the bottom of friend having no stomach to hold party

indicators.note: the shortened word wraps round the party, holding it inside
the stomach is the middle of the body, so the word friend loses its middle letters

parts.note: an at-home is a party held in one's own house

explanation.surface: A slimmed-down friend hosting a party: perhaps a mystery solved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no stomach' strips FRIEND to its outer letters FD; 'to hold' puts AT HOME (an old word for a reception at one's house) between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to understand it fully, as if sounding its depth.

clue.text: Quickly encompassing end of life — euphemism for "dead"

indicators.note: the phrase for quickly surrounds the letter from life

parts.note: at pace means quickly

indicators.note: the end of the word life is its last letter

explanation.surface: A life rushed to its end, softened into a gentle phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encompassing' puts E, the end of 'life', inside AT PACE.
explanation.definitionFit: At peace is a gentle phrase for someone who has died, as in 'now at peace'.

clue.text: Looking wrong, yet red hair is in the family

indicators.note: something looking wrong is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Red hair looks out of place but runs in the family anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking wrong' rearranges YETREDHAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereditary traits are passed down through generations, so they run in families.

clue.text: Skulk around, not the first to kiss

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for kissing is left off

parts.note: to smooch is to kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: Someone skulks about, not being the first to go in for a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' drops the S of SMOOCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch around is to loiter aimlessly, lurking or idling about.

clue.text: Time for one obscure worry? No time

parts.note: to dim something is to obscure it

indicators.note: no here means without, so the time letter is taken out

parts.note: tension is anxiety or worry

explanation.surface: A dark worry with no time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No time' removes T from TENSION.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is often called the fourth dimension, alongside length, width and height.

clue.text: Start to sketch possibly libellous poster, no hurry

indicators.note: the start of the word sketch is its first letter

parts.note: an internet troll posts abusive messages, possibly libellous

explanation.surface: An artist begins drawing a defamatory poster, taking their time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poster' looks like a printed bill but is someone who posts online.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely walk, taken in no hurry.

clue.text: One goes with hose that's found in gutter

definitions.text: One goes with hose that's found in gutter

parts.words: One goes with hose that's found in gutter
parts.note: a Tudor jacket worn with hose; and the middle of the word gutter shows a pair of Ts, a repeated T

explanation.surface: Something you might find lying in a gutter goes with a hosepipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' looks like a garden hosepipe, but it is old-fashioned tights or breeches: 'doublet and hose' was Tudor menswear. The letters TT in 'gutter' are a double T.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a close-fitting jacket traditionally worn with hose in Elizabethan dress.

clue.text: Act under compulsion to cancel church Mass

indicators.note: the church letters are cancelled and the Mass letter takes their place

parts.note: perforce means by necessity, because one is forced
CE is the Church of England
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Someone forced by law to call off a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cancel' marks the swap: the church letters go and the Mass letter replaces them. 'Mass' sits naturally beside 'church' but is the physics symbol, not a service.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform is to act, as on a stage.

clue.text: Great success of small group setting leader back

indicators.note: the first letter of the group's word is moved back to the end

parts.note: a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: A small band's hit came when they dropped their frontman to the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting leader back' moves the T of TRIO to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot is informal for a huge hit, as in 'the show was a riot'.

clue.text: Not always on hand, went travelling

indicators.note: the letters travel about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who was not always around had gone off on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges ONHANDWENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done now and then happens occasionally, so not every time.

clue.text: Operating in colour that's extra strong

indicators.note: the phrase for operating goes inside the colour

parts.note: red is a colour
a law in force is operating

explanation.surface: Something running inside a coloured casing is particularly tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinforced means strengthened with extra support, as in reinforced concrete.

clue.text: Endlessly tough for each general author

indicators.note: without its end, the last letter of the word for tough goes

parts.note: hard means tough
per means for each, as in 'per person'
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A hard-nosed writer who has served as a military commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops the D of HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Harper Lee was the American novelist who wrote To Kill a Mockingbird.

clue.text: Hands up for success in school sport

parts.note: a high school is a secondary school
fives is a handball game played in a court, at some British public schools

explanation.surface: Pupils raise their hands after winning at school sport.
explanation.walkthrough: FIVES is a British handball game played against walls, mainly at public schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A high five is a celebratory slap of raised palms after a success.

clue.text: I hadn't turned round paintings

indicators.note: the phrase is turned round to be read backwards

parts.note: I hadn't done something means I did not

explanation.surface: Someone denies having turned the pictures round to face the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hadn't' expands to I DID NOT, shortened to I D NOT; 'turned round' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tondi (singular tondo) are circular paintings or reliefs, a Renaissance form.

clue.text: One's taken wrong line in the dark, lacking this?

definitions.text: One's taken wrong line in the dark, lacking this?

indicators.note: taken the wrong way means the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the word one, with 's meaning 'is' as a link

indicators.note: the line letter goes inside the word for darkness

parts.note: night is the time of darkness

explanation.surface: Someone has wandered off the path at night because there was no lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken wrong' scrambles the word one; 'in' puts the line letter inside the dark. Read whole, a missing street lamp explains the wrong turn, so the clue is its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A neon light is a glowing gas-filled tube, the kind of lamp that would have shown the way.

clue.text: Board to manage progress

definitions.meaning: to ... a bus or train is to board it
'how are you getting on?' asks how you are managing
to ... in life is to make progress

explanation.surface: A company board tries to drive the business forward.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb get on has all three senses: embarking, coping, and advancing.

clue.text: Some hours which minutes on piano might stretch into?

definitions.text: Some hours which minutes on piano might stretch into?

parts.words: Some hours which minutes on piano might stretch into?
parts.note: minutes are M, piano is P; M put on P (after it) makes PM, the letters for the hours after midday

explanation.surface: Piano practice meant to last minutes drags on for hours.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a long practice session; cryptically, M after P is PM, and PM is the period the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: PM, post meridiem, labels the hours after midday until evening.

clue.text: Fix up say to go beyond Scottish island

indicators.note: the reversed letters come after the island, going past it

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, which say also means

explanation.surface: Fix up a trip, for example, beyond a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix up' looks like the definition; 'up' belongs to the wordplay, turning EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange something is to fix or settle it, as in fixing a date.

clue.text: Not be serious about woman as PA

indicators.note: the word for trifling goes about the woman's name

parts.note: to toy with something is to treat it lightly
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman working as a personal assistant is told not to be so serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PA' looks like a personal assistant but is a public-address system; Tannoy is the British brand name for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tannoy is a trademark used in Britain for any public-address loudspeaker system.

clue.text: One adds zest as Liberal, in showing partiality

indicators.note: the Liberal letter goes inside the word for showing partiality

parts.note: favouring someone means showing them partiality

explanation.surface: A politician brings energy as a Liberal while being accused of bias.
explanation.definitionFit: A flavouring is an ingredient added to give food a taste, much as zest does.

clue.text: Cavities in human trachea

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words human trachea

explanation.surface: Anatomy: hollow spaces found in a person's windpipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Antra is the plural of antrum, an anatomical term for a body cavity or chamber.

clue.text: Dressed heel, nicked by end of chisel

indicators.note: the cad is cut into, as if nicked by a blade, and the chisel's letter goes inside

parts.note: a heel is a cad, a man who behaves dishonourably

indicators.note: the end of the word chisel is its last letter

explanation.surface: A shoe heel finished off with a nick from a chisel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heel' looks like part of a shoe, which suits the chisel, but it means a cad. 'nicked by' puts L into CAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad is an old past participle of clothe, meaning wearing clothes.

clue.text: Healing process getting both sides in debate to vote

indicators.note: both sides of the word debate are its outer letters

parts.note: X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Healing divisions by getting both sides of a debate to vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both sides in debate' gives DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A detox is a course of treatment clearing toxins from the body, a recovery process.

clue.text: One share in decision that's a surprise

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to have a say is to share in a decision

explanation.surface: Someone surprised to be given a part in a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: 'I say!' is a dated British exclamation of surprise.

clue.text: Inspired by a new religious centre

parts.note: vatic means prophetic, inspired as a seer is

explanation.surface: Someone is moved by a fresh place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: VATIC (an uncommon word for prophetic) takes A and N after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican in Rome is the seat of the Pope and heart of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: As soon as clocked in the workplace can be heard

indicators.note: the phrase as spoken matches the answer's sound

parts.note: on site means at the place of work

explanation.surface: Clocking in at work is something you can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clocked' looks like punching a time card at work but means spotted: on sight is the moment something is seen.
explanation.definitionFit: On sight means immediately upon being seen, and clocked is slang for noticed.

clue.text: Course a little short for its country's patron

indicators.note: cutting the place name a little short removes its final letter

parts.note: St Andrews is the famous golf course in Scotland, the home of golf

explanation.surface: A golf course is a bit short for championship play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little short' trims the final S from ST ANDREWS; 'its' points back to Scotland, home of the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Andrew is the patron saint of Scotland, where the course lies.

clue.text: Announced changes of course on crime sentencing rules

indicators.note: said aloud, the phrase is heard as the answer

parts.note: changes of course are tacks, as in sailing; crime is sin; tacks put after sin gives this phrase

explanation.surface: Announced reforms to how judges sentence criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentencing' looks legal but means building sentences; 'Announced' says SIN TACKS aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Syntax is the set of grammatical rules governing how sentences are put together.
